invariants.note: Single SWAP kernel remains unchanged; this is a runtime/coupler service seam.
No file, format, parsing, path or file-unit dependency is introduced.
External groundwater committed state remains outside SWAP state, parameters and forcing.
Only lightweight checkpoint/candidate handles cross the seam; no groundwater state is persisted per SWAP column.
Backend trial scratch remains backend/worker owned and is not persistent SWAP state.
Opaque integer handles do not constrain internal backend storage layout or batching.
Checkpoint, multi-trial, discard and single-commit semantics are explicit; rejected trials do not publish committed state.
Multiple trial candidates can start from one committed checkpoint without changing the physical origin.
The service consumes generic finite increasing [t0,t1] windows and has no calendar-unit semantics.
Non-midnight fractional windows are qualified; no fixed coupling-window duration is encoded.
Transactional groundwater-side coupling support is explicit runtime functionality.
The service reuses the typed F-GC17 groundwater window and outward groundwater flux convention.
No mass tolerance or bookkeeping approximation is introduced by the service contract.
Interface-sensitivity transport remains independent and available downstream.
The service seam does not prescribe extra SWAP trajectories or a multi-run production path.
Service handles are lightweight and compatible with many logical columns and shared backend workers.
No 1:1 relationship between SWAP columns and groundwater cells is encoded.
Deep-vadose remains an optional external composition and is not embedded here.
The contract does not create, destroy or remap stored water between components.
No soil-water solver implementation is referenced by the groundwater service seam.
No SWAP process physics is duplicated or moved into the groundwater service.
No HeadCalc internals or arrays are referenced.
Groundwater service lifecycle is distinct from physical SWAP options and numerical solver policy.
No hidden retry ladder, unbounded work or silent fallback is introduced.
Reference mode remains available and unchanged.
Service ID, lineage, origin revision, candidate revision, window and failure status are explicit diagnostics.
The service exists and costs work only when groundwater coupling is invoked.
External groundwater composition remains runtime/coupler-owned; SWAP does not know the external model type.
No MODFLOW type, file format, midnight start, daily duration or hidden external-model assumption is introduced.
The change was explicitly audited against all architecture invariants before closeout.
